boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Camp Wildcat (Rockcastle Hills) record (October 21, 1861) in Operations in Eastern Kentucky [September-December 1861]. Zollicoffer's advance from Cumberland Ford and his retreat to Cumberland Ford are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field gives the Union garrison and Schoepf's brigade about 7,000 and names Zollicoffer's brigade without a figure; the live field reads US 7,000 and CS 0. NPS says Garrard reported being outnumbered seven to one before Schoepf brought the total to about 7,000. Schoepf says three prisoners each put the enemy at about 7,000. Zollicoffer says the enemy's camp was said to be 7,000 strong with large reserves and, on October 26, that nine regiments were there.
claims.rationale: Each side attributes about 7,000 to the other; the CWSAC Union figure is not traced to a return. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live CS zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory; NPS says the Federals repelled the attacks and the Confederates withdrew in the night. Schoepf says the enemy fully retreated toward London; Zollicoffer describes a reconnaissance in force after which he fell back.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 78 (US 25; CS 53); the live field reads 96 (US 43; CS 53). Schoepf reports 4 killed and 18 wounded and set the enemy's loss at 30 killed, adding a citizen's report that they acknowledged 100 killed. Zollicoffer reports 42 wounded and 11 killed and missing and 21 prisoners taken.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The CS 53 equals Zollicoffer's 42 and 11; that equality is not independent confirmation.

open_questions: Thomas's No. 1 dispatches (which relay Schoepf), Coburn's No. 3 and Newman's No. 6 reports, Schoepf's pencil note (not printed), returns and maps remain deferred. No nineteenth-century history covering the action was selected; this is a two-report or two-family first pass.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Schoepf's October 22 and 23, 1861 reports are one family of interested Union accounts. Zollicoffer's September 19 and October 20-26, 1861 reports are one family of interested Confederate accounts (the same author for Barbourville and Camp Wildcat). Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
